cards.front: What is the difference between negative liberty and positive liberty? How does the Indian Constitution reflect both, and is liberty absolute in India?
cards.back:
Negative libertyPositive liberty
MeaningFreedom from external restraint – an area where no one interferesFreedom to develop oneself – having the conditions and capacity to act
Role of the StateStay out; protect the individual from interferenceAct – remove obstacles like poverty and illiteracy
In the ConstitutionMost Fundamental Rights, e.g. Art. 19 freedoms, Art. 21DPSPs and enabling rights, e.g. Art. 21A education, Art. 39(a) livelihood, Art. 41 work

Not absolute: Art. 19(2)–(6) allow reasonable restrictions on grounds such as public order, security of the State and morality. The Preamble speaks of liberty of thought, expression, belief, faith and worship.

⚠ Common mistake: Equating liberty with ‘no limits’. In political theory and in the Constitution, liberty means absence of unreasonable restraint, not absence of all restraint.

cards.front: The original Constitution had 8 Schedules. Which amendment added each of the 9th, 10th, 11th and 12th Schedules, and what does each contain?
cards.back:
ScheduleAdded byContents
9th1st Amendment, 1951Land reform and other laws protected from challenge on FR grounds (Art. 31B)
10th52nd Amendment, 1985Anti-defection law
11th73rd Amendment, 199229 subjects for Panchayats
12th74th Amendment, 199218 subjects for Municipalities

⚠ Common mistake: Linking the 10th Schedule to the 42nd or 91st Amendment. It came with the 52nd (1985); the 91st (2003) only removed the ‘split’ exception.

cards.front: Name four important rights outside Part III. Can you move the Supreme Court under Article 32 if one of them is violated?
cards.back:
ArticleRight
265 (Part XII)No tax shall be levied or collected except by authority of law
300A (Part XII)No person shall be deprived of property save by authority of law
301 (Part XIII)Freedom of trade, commerce and intercourse throughout India
326 (Part XV)Elections to Lok Sabha and State Assemblies on the basis of adult suffrage

Remedy: these are constitutional/legal rights, not Fundamental Rights. Art. 32 is not available; the remedy is a writ under Art. 226 or an ordinary suit.

⚠ Common mistake: Treating the right to property or the right to vote as Fundamental Rights. Both are outside Part III, so Art. 32 cannot be used directly.

cards.front: Which new Directive Principles were added to Part IV by later amendments? Give the Article and the amendment for each.
cards.back:
AmendmentNew DPSP
42nd (1976)Art. 39(f) healthy development of children; Art. 39A equal justice and free legal aid; Art. 43A workers’ participation in management; Art. 48A protection of environment, forests and wildlife
44th (1978)Art. 38(2) minimise inequalities in income, status, facilities and opportunities
86th (2002)Art. 45 changed to early childhood care and education up to six years
97th (2011)Art. 43B promotion of co-operative societies

⚠ Common mistake: Assuming free legal aid (Art. 39A) or environment protection (Art. 48A) were in the original Constitution. Both came with the 42nd Amendment.
